newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: At least 60 hurt in Bangladesh campus violence.
newsitem.headline: At least 60 hurt in Bangladesh campus violence.

text.p: At least 60 students, teachers and police were injured when militant Islamic activists went on a rampage at the Rajshahi University in northern Bangladesh on Saturday, police said on Sunday.

They said members of Islami Chhatra Shibir, the student wing of the fundamentalist Jamaat-e-Islami party, hurled hand-made bombs at student dormitories and teachers' homes on the campus. The activists also ransacked administrative offices during the six-hour rampage.
The Islamists were opposing proposed changes in admission rules, university officials told reporters without elaborating.
Shibir activists wearing black masks stormed the residence of Vice Chancellor Abdul Khaleq and assaulted his children and relatives.
They also fired guns at police, attacked a bank booth and damaged some 35 university vehicles by puncturing tyres.
Three injured policemen were sent to hospital in critical condition, police said.
The Daily Independent newspaper, quoting witnesses, said hundreds of gunshots were fired and dozens of small explosives set off during the violence, which panicked students and residents.
Police took control of the campus on Saturday night, local residents said.
Last week, police in southern Chittagong city, another stronghold of the Islamists, unearthed a large cache of illegal firearms and ammunition during a raid on a Shibir den.
Police said they had announced rewards for information on the whereabouts of a local Shibir leader, Nasir (one name), who was wanted on charges ranging from keeping illegal weapons to killings.
Campus violence kills dozens in Bangladesh every year.
President Shahabuddin Ahmed earlier this year called for a temporary ban on student politics to restore calm on campuses. But no one has yet responded to his plea.
